    Student progress tracker¶

    Retain the useful fall/winter/spring growth conversation, but track taught objectives rather than enthusiasm or generic participation. October 2026. Use assessment, rubrics and Local Standards.

    Lesson evidence roster¶

    Student Date/grade/unit/lesson Objective/local code Exact action/words or artifact Mode/access support ½/¾ or NE Feedback/next check
    [One row per child; extend to actual enrollment, including 25] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Levels: 1 Beginning, 2 Developing, 3 Meets Expectation, 4 Extends Learning. Use the lesson's specific descriptors. NE means no adequate evidence yet (absence, unavailable equipment, missed check); it is not a zero. Ordinary read-aloud, gesture, bilingual response, scribe and motor assistance do not lower achievement. Record conceptual hints separately.

    Termly growth summary¶

    Student/objective/local code Fall evidence/date/level Winter evidence/date/level Spring evidence/date/level Next teaching
    [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Examples of appropriate evidence by grade, not new official benchmarks:

    Grade Possible individual evidence when corresponding objective taught
    K Points/sorts by an observed feature; shows a two-action sequence; tells one detail
    1 Names the problem/user; compares two results; explains one design choice
    2 Records an equal-condition comparison; explains a changed sequence
    3 Shows common test conditions and links one redesign to the result
    4 Measures in the specified unit and uses results to justify an improvement
    5 Compares two designs using taught criteria/constraints
    6 Defends a choice with evidence, cost/tradeoff and a taught ethical consideration

    This is not an independent progression specification: use the shared grade progression and local definitions for expected outcomes. Real program/robot execution is only recorded when actually demonstrated on a working device. Never fill those cells from an unplugged activity.

    Workload and privacy¶

    During hands-on time sweep the roster; pair a simultaneous point/show/draw exit response with short targeted conversations. At 25, record unobserved children NE and collect later rather than assuming all groups mastered the concept. Review at project completion and termly; do not require daily long checklists. At expected-mastery checkpoints, retain two dated observations on separate occasions as required by Local Standards, including an individual demonstration and changed context/follow-up explanation. Both must meet the target; one lesson rating is not end-of-grade mastery. Store named records under the school's actual privacy practice. Do not publish names, scores or photographs in newsletters without verified permission.

    Behavior/engagement notes may inform support but remain separate from subject mastery. Report "measured the span accurately; next compare repeated trials," not "participates well, therefore proficient."

    C-STREAM substitute teacher guide¶

    C = Catholic identity, R = religion/faith integration, A = arts including music, M = mathematics. Thank you for leading hands-on learning. October 2026. Use the actual scheduled lesson, not a generic assurance that every old lesson is ready. Readiness review.

    Twenty minutes before class¶

    Minutes Do this
    0-4 Read objective, background/vocabulary and native timed steps; identify each child's evidence prompt
    4-8 Find the kit at the location supplied by school; count student/team/class/teacher items for enrollment
    8-12 Read SAFETY; check accommodations, materials condition and actual school emergency/office contact
    12-16 Perform the exact lesson model/pretest, then place counted trays and assign roles
    16-20 Draw/read aloud short steps; rehearse individual check, cleanup and the named fallback

    School must fill lesson/date [ ], kit/actual location [ ], office/contact [ ], accommodations [ ], emergency instructions [ ] before handoff. Do not assume "STREAM closet," iPads, apps, loan kits or a quick-reference card exists.

    Grade 3 example: rebuilt Week 10 Bridge Engineering. Use its precise quantities/span/load/check and 40-minute period. If its kit or prep test fails, use the fallback below and record the changed objective. This guide does not certify all legacy lessons.

    SAFETY: stop rather than improvise¶

    No button cells, latex balloons, projectile activities or neodymium magnets in K. No unknown chemicals, food experiments, glass, hot surfaces, unsafe cold exposure or electrical repair. Teacher controls batteries/clip leads/small loads. Do not use unfamiliar electric/magnetic equipment without a verified pretest. Stop, isolate unsafe materials, move to a seated safe task and notify the responsible school adult. Injury, suspected ingestion of a battery/magnet or other urgent danger requires the school's emergency escalation immediately. Do not send pupils hunting for missing dangerous parts.

    Fallback A: paper structure comparison¶

    Objective: Compare flat and folded paper under the same span and load. Big idea: Shape can affect a structure; a fair comparison keeps test conditions the same. Catholic connection: Reliable design serves people; shared resources are used responsibly. No "God is an engineer" comparison. Technology Requirement: None. Difficulty: introductory comparison. Prep: 10 minutes if counted stock/supports exist; cleanup included below. Vocabulary: span = gap between supports; load = what a structure supports; compare = notice how results are alike/different.

    Background/misconception: Folded and flat paper may respond differently. The result can be the same under a small load; report that honestly. A collapse is information, not failure of the student. If asked why a fold matters, show the changed shape; do not promise that every fold always improves it.

    Scope/material Rate 10 pupils 15 20 25
    Student response paper (or oral response) 1/child 10 15 20 25
    Team paper 2/team 8 10 14 18
    Team index-card test loads 10/team 40 50 70 90
    Team ruler 1/team 4 5 7 9
    Stable support books/blocks 2/team 8 10 14 18
    Teacher 2 demonstration sheets, 10 cards, timer, evidence roster One class set in addition to team issue quantities

    Pencils/crayons are school basics. Total paper at 25 = 25 + 18 + 2 = 45 sheets; total cards = 90 + 10 = 100. No scissors, coins, tape, devices or donations. Books/supports must be confirmed; without them use fallback B, not an unsafe stack.

    Before class: Set stable supports 10 cm apart on each desk; lay one sheet flat across. Fold the second lengthwise into an accordion with adult modeling. Try adding cards one by one at the center in both tests; reset with the same gap and count. Test before class; reduce the gap if neither supports even one card and record that shared change. No escalating to heavy falling weights. K adult places loads; child still predicts/points/compares.

    Exact native timing (choose the grade column)¶

    Step K 25 1-2 30 3-4 40 5-6 45 What to do/say
    Hook/purpose 0-3 0-3 0-4 0-4 "What might a fold change?" Explain objective and stewardship
    Model/vocabulary/safety 3-7 3-8 4-10 4-11 Align supports, show flat/folded examples, demonstrate one load placement
    Build/test first comparison 7-14 8-18 10-24 11-27 Students take turns placing paper/cards; count or point to result
    Improve/retest 14-19 18-23 24-32 27-36 Change one paper shape; keep gap/load placement. "What stayed the same?"
    Individual check 19-22 23-27 32-37 36-41 "Show the result. What stayed the same in the test?"
    Cleanup/close 22-25 27-30 37-40 41-45 Count cards/rulers/supports, retain dry paper, clear desks, brief thanks

    Meets: Each child identifies the observed comparison (including equal results) and shows one common condition. For K, adult reads/models and accepts pointing/gesture. Use Show, Try, Tell. Support: Pre-fold paper, steady supports, scribe or allow a large gesture. Challenge: Repeat the comparison and explain whether it supports the first result; older pupils can compare equal-material versions without untaught ratios. At 25: Nine seated teams, rotating turns; check children during tests plus simultaneous show/draw exit. Mark unobserved evidence NE and leave a follow-up. Troubleshoot: Sliding supports -> stabilize or stop that test; equal results -> record them, not "wrong"; time short -> stop new construction, keep check/cleanup. Family copy: "We compared paper structures using the same gap and loads. Ask: 'What stayed the same, and what changed?' Optional: discuss a folded object already nearby. No home project needed."

    Fallback B: no devices, no consumable supplies, or unsafe weather¶

    Objective: Make and distinguish a direct observation from a guess. Materials: A familiar safe classroom object/view already present; no handling of hazardous objects. Technology: None. Prep: 2 minutes. Vocabulary/background: Observe = notice directly; guess/inference = an idea that needs more evidence. "Looks wooden" does not prove material composition.

    Follow the same native timing columns above: 1. Hook: "What can we actually notice about this desk/door/window view?" 2. Model one observation and one inference; safety: seated, no climbing/touching. 3. Each child notices/points/tells one feature; partners compare. 4. Identify which claim can be checked by looking; refine it. 5. Each child shows one observable feature (older pupils distinguish a guess). 6. Restore room, finish the evidence notes and close.

    Meets: Child points/names an observable feature; for a stated older-grade inference objective also explains why a guess needs evidence. Read aloud, model, allow gesture/gaze/home-language response. Challenge: propose a safe way to check a guess. Record objective change; no claim of engineering/programming mastery. Cleanup: no materials to collect; reset seating and leave evidence/NE. Family: "We practiced observing carefully. Ask: 'What did you notice directly?'" At -10 F remain indoors; if there is no safe view, use an ordinary indoor object.

    Device/supply contingency and return note¶

    Paper algorithms preserve sequence/debugging concepts, not real programming or robot-operation mastery. Defer those objectives if devices fail; do not invent accounts or app permissions. Technology Plan.

    Leave lesson/steps completed, actual individual evidence or NE, objectives changed/deferred, restock counts, broken parts OUT OF SERVICE, safety/source questions and the next check. Named evidence stays under school privacy practice. See handoff template and Local Standards; official alignment and unverified Church/supplier claims are VERIFICATION REQUIRED.

    Kindergarten reference routines¶

    Read this page with the selected lesson. It supplies reusable routines, not permission to omit that lesson's exact materials, test or safety instructions. Every minimum pathway works indoors, without independent reading or a device.

    Twenty-minute substitute gate¶

    1. 0-4 minutes: read the objective, background, test and individual check.
    2. 4-8: locate actual supplies; count the selected enrollment column.
    3. 8-12: inspect materials and confirm accommodations, school contact and any adult-only preparation. A supply estimate is not an owned kit.
    4. 12-16: perform the lesson's demonstration/pretest and distribute kits.
    5. 16-20: draw directions and rehearse the check and cleanup.

    If a safety condition or exact material is missing, use only the lesson's named alternative. Record the different/deferred objective; do not improvise unknown substances, electrical connections, outdoor exposure or a human trial.

    Common teacher kit: one classroom timer/clock, paper roster and school pencil or school-approved equivalent writing tool, for any enrollment. No pupil device is implied. The audit indexes this common kit separately from student supplies. Adult cutting, secured AA cells and Winter Science tongs are indexed where the selected lesson needs them. Prepared-resource prices do not include these tools or imply verified school stock.

    Teams and quantities¶

    Pupils Active pair/trio teams Kit budget Additional reserve
    10 5 pairs 5 0
    15 6 pairs + 1 trio 8 1
    20 10 pairs 10 0
    25 11 pairs + 1 trio 13 1

    Lesson tables use the kit budget, not a lone child working in a "pair." Unless a lesson explicitly adds teacher supplies, demonstrate with one budgeted kit and return it before practice. Never count a reserve twice.

    With fewer kits, use groups no larger than three: ⅘/7/9 groups respectively (2 trios + 2 pairs; 5 trios; 6 trios + 1 pair; 7 trios + 2 pairs). Recalculate the per-kit issue quantities. Preserve the test and every child's turn; do not change a learning target merely to fit a materials shortage. If individual turns cannot fit, record missing evidence and schedule follow-up.

    Nonreader directions and access¶

    Demonstrate one action, say it, let children show it, then add the next action. Use large drawings of an eye, hands, two arrows and a return box. No printout or icon-reading skill is assumed. A child can point, describe, dictate, build or direct an adult to act. Ask permission before physical assistance.

    Swap chooser/builder, tester and reporter roles during work. A third child gets a full choice and test turn, not permanent observation duty. Provide a seated route, large parts and a quieter/visual alternative as needed.

    Individual evidence without a serial exit line¶

    Prepare a roster with the lesson's two or three observable checks. Begin checking during 8-17 minutes, then finish during 17-21 while partners work. Thirteen combined minutes provide an average of about 31 seconds per child at 25 enrollment; actual processing needs may require later follow-up. Record not yet / prompted / independent separately for each check. Do not convert an unobserved response into a pass.

    Show what was tested, distinguish prediction from result, and ask one real question. Group products, compliance, handwriting and artistic polish are not mastery. A failed prototype can still produce excellent evidence. The local progression's mastery checkpoints need two dated individual observations; one lesson or a certificate cannot establish grade readiness.

    Common safety and cleanup¶

    Use teacher-inspected large paper pieces and sound blocks, seated desk tests, no student weight on models and no food/unknown nature materials. Do not taste, sniff closely, collect nests or view the Sun. No small magnets, button cells, lasers, flames, latex balloons, projectiles or mouth-contact instruments. Adults control scissors, batteries and wet setup. Keep paths/exits clear. Follow actual school allergy, hygiene, emergency and accommodation procedures.

    At 21-25 minutes, stop the test; count reusable pieces into their labeled kit; cap school-approved glue; retain dated evidence; flatten dry scrap for reuse/recycling; clear tables. Store models by kit number rather than publishing student names. Wet lessons use their own hygiene/cleanup plan.

    Catholic connection and source use¶

    Teach honest evidence, care of creation, dignity, inclusion and service. Prayer is optional according to the school's practice and is not a mastery check. Classroom applications are local, not official religious standards. Use the verified Church teaching register: CCC 159 (faith/reason), 1702/1704 (dignity/reason), 2415-2418 (creation care), 2427-2428 (work), 2468-2469 (truth). Do not attribute original classroom language to a saint or Scripture. An approved religion reading is an optional addition, not a scientific explanation.

    Continuity and family communication¶

    Keep one dated sheet per child when a lesson specifies it. Use an envelope by class/meeting; no expensive journal is required. Multi-meeting models stay at school. If prior work is unavailable, use the lesson's fresh-evidence route, never invent a past result.

    Newsletter statements describe what was actually taught and observed. Family questions are optional and ungraded. No home device, purchase, donation, collection, adult teaching or homework supplies an essential assessment.

    C-STREAM FAQ and troubleshooting¶

    October 2026. Start with Quick Start and a completed lesson template. Generalist teachers can teach a clear lesson; not every legacy file is ready. Confirm rotation/calendar and the actual lesson rather than promising no repetition or universal substitute-readiness.

    Time and classroom management¶

    Running long? Stop new construction, retain the individual check and cleanup, store dry labeled work and continue next meeting. Do not delete evidence collection to add an extra activity or prayer.

    Finished early? Ask for a repeated fair test, alternative constraint or explanation of evidence. Faster pupils are not automatically unpaid helpers.

    Students excited/arguing? Give instructions before materials, use a stop signal, assign builder/tester/reporter and rotate actual turns. Ask each to show an idea and test alternatives under the same conditions. Refer persistent behavior/safety concerns through actual school procedures.

    A child needs more time? Model one step, reduce choices, pre-cut/larger materials, allow gesture/voice/scribe/quiet or seated response. Keep the concept criterion unless documenting an explicit objective change.

    Missing supplies or technology¶

    Problem Safe response Learning limit
    Building blocks absent Paper/cardstock/sticks with a stated new constraint Compare evidence; do not silently claim identical load capacity
    Robot/app/host unavailable Desk-grid arrow cards and pointer Sequence/debugging concepts only; execution/robot mastery deferred
    Internet absent Teacher-vetted read-aloud source or confirmed offline tool Actual online/source-navigation objective may change
    Some devices work Document turn/reset time, smaller test rotations or more meetings Each child needs individual real-device evidence if that is O1
    Electrical gear damaged Switch off/disconnect; OUT OF SERVICE; safe paper-path model Paper path is not practical circuit-building mastery
    No safe materials or weather Seated observation fallback Record actual observation objective, not unperformed investigation

    Do not open personal accounts, install unapproved apps, bypass safeguards or improvise power supplies. Technology Plan. Borrowing lead times/fees/stock are VERIFICATION REQUIRED, not guaranteed two-week free access. Library planning.

    Assessment¶

    How do I grade? Use the objective -> prompt -> success condition -> individual evidence chain. Project rubric. Participation, effort, handwriting, neatness and confidence are not mastery. An artistic criterion is used only for an explicit arts objective.

    What if the model fails? A child can still explain valid evidence and redesign. A successful team model does not prove each member understands. NE means not yet evidenced; unobserved/absent/device-blocked is not a zero.

    How much paperwork? Short roster evidence during work plus one exit check; review termly with Progress Tracker. Named records/photos follow verified school privacy/consent practice; do not assume a digital account or public portfolio.

    Faith, arts and grade differences¶

    Faith connection feels forced? Use a concrete Catholic decision about dignity, truth, stewardship or service. R identifies the explicit reflection. Prayer supports but does not substitute for this purpose. Verify Church quotations, biographies and standards; never make an experiment theological proof.

    Hard science/faith question? Acknowledge uncertainty, distinguish observation from belief/interpretation and consult the verified source record or appropriate school faith educator. Avoid a simplistic "science only how, faith only why" rule or "God is an engineer" analogy.

    What does A mean? Arts including music: observational drawing, composition, visual communication, form, rhythmic phrases and performance, not just digital art/decoration. M means mathematics.

    K cannot read? Use Show, Try, Tell. An attempt is welcome but does not automatically demonstrate the concept. Assess pointing/sorting/building/telling with the same explicit success condition.

    Mixed grades / older students need challenge? Same materials can support different evidence expectations; use the shared progression and actual prerequisites. Add repeat trials, constraints, measurement or tradeoffs, not untaught ratio work or leadership as a substitute for subject learning.

    Safety and families¶

    No button cells, latex balloons or projectiles in the core; no neodymium magnets in K. Stop unsafe activities, isolate hazards and contact the school's responsible adult. Possible battery/magnet ingestion needs urgent emergency escalation. Use indoor alternatives in unsafe Minnesota conditions.

    No routine homework, required donations or home purchase/device. Explain concept + action + evidence + Catholic choice using family communication.

    Parent Resources

    Parent communication guide¶

    Use one family communication system and newsletter template; K-6 unit examples and specific oral questions are supplied there. Retain plain language, welcoming invitations, positive evidence notes and family feedback. No routine homework or donation prerequisite. October 2026.

    Introduction letter (copy and personalize)¶

    Dear Families,

    In C-STREAM, children learn through observing, building, measuring, testing, improving, composing and explaining. C means Catholic identity; R is religion/faith integration; A includes arts and music; M means mathematics. Our Catholic purpose includes dignity, stewardship, truthful reasoning and using gifts to serve others. Faith reflection does not replace scientific evidence. Art includes genuine choices about pattern, form, sound and communication, not just decorating a product.

    We use hands-on materials first and devices when they add meaningful learning. Every child has school-provided supplies and classroom work time. There is no routine C-STREAM homework, purchase, device or donation requirement. Newsletters include a specific question you can ask and an optional no-purchase activity. Your child may show learning by speaking, pointing, drawing, modeling or recording, with needed access support.

    Questions? Contact [actual teacher/school-approved contact].

    Project launch letter¶

    Project/unit/date: [ ] Objective: [ ] Classroom meetings: [ ] What children will do: [Specific actions and individual evidence.] Catholic decision: [Dignity/stewardship/service/truth.] School-provided materials and work time: [ ] Optional event: [Confirmed invitation and in-class non-attendance route.] Ask: "[Actual result/choice question.]" Home participation: Optional conversation only; no home research/building, purchased display board, donation or account required.

    Positive evidence note¶

    Dear [Family], Today [child] demonstrated [objective] by [actual action/explanation]. Next we will practice [specific next step]. Thank you for encouraging curiosity. [Teacher/contact]

    Keep individual notes private using the school's actual approved method. Do not publicly post names, scores, photographs or identifiable work without verified school consent/privacy arrangements.

    Showcases and family feedback¶

    Use Student Project Rubric for selected objective-linked evidence, not fixed percentages for attractive displays, confidence, family-funded materials or participation. Work is completed in class; family attendance is optional. Students may show/tell/draw with support. Ask families: "Was the learning clear?" "Was the optional activity accessible?" "What questions remain?" Event planning: STREAM Night.

    Source questions about Church teaching, scientists, official standards or diocesan policy are VERIFICATION REQUIRED. Local codes link to Local Standards; they are not official accreditation.

    Weekly parent sheet template¶

    Use the common newsletter template at unit launch/completion or for a major lesson. The family communication system supplies ready-to-adapt examples for K, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6.

    Copy for families¶

    This week/unit in C-STREAM - grade/unit/date: [ ] What we explored: [ ] What students did: [Actual observation/build/test/measure/compose/program; say unplugged if no program executed.] What they learned: [Specific concept and evidence.] Our Catholic connection: [Actual dignity/stewardship/service decision.] Ask your child: "[Specific question answerable orally.]" Try this at home, optional: [Short no-purchase safe activity; no device, account, outdoor exposure, photo, submission or special equipment required.] Coming next/contact: [Confirmed school-approved information.]

    C is Catholic identity; R is religion/faith integration; A is arts including music; M is mathematics. No comparisons that make God an engineer/scientist or turn a physical result into theological proof. No compulsory scientist spotlight. Church quotations/biographies require verification before copying.

    No routine homework. School supplies all required learning materials; donations and optional activities never affect participation or grades. No identifiable student names/images/scores without the verified school consent/privacy process.

    🙋 C-STREAM Volunteer Guide¶

    Location: Our Lady of the Prairie Catholic School · Belle Plaine, MN · Archdiocese of Saint Paul and Minneapolis

    Thank you for volunteering in our C-STREAM classroom! This guide will help you support hands-on, faith-integrated STEM learning.

    October 2026 safety/access note: The teacher retains responsibility. Confirm school screening, safeguarding, supervision, emergency and privacy requirements before volunteering; any claimed Archdiocesan requirement needs source verification. Share only accommodation information necessary for your assigned role. No button cells, latex balloons or projectile activities; no neodymium magnets in K. Do not repair electrical gear or handle batteries without the teacher's assigned procedure. Stop hazards and notify the teacher; suspected battery/magnet ingestion requires immediate emergency escalation. Use materials kit counts and the substitute safety guide.

    🎯 Your Role as a Volunteer¶

    You ARE here to:¶

    ✅ Support students as they work
    ✅ Encourage when things don't work the first time
    ✅ Ask questions that help students think
    ✅ Assist with materials and supplies
    ✅ Celebrate effort and creativity
    ✅ Model curiosity and wonder

    You are NOT expected to:¶

    ❌ Know all the answers (it's okay to say "Let's find out together!")
    ❌ Do the work for students
    ❌ Teach the lesson (the teacher leads instruction)
    ❌ Grade or evaluate student work
    ❌ Discipline students (refer behavior issues to the teacher)

    📅 Before You Arrive¶

    What to Know¶

    • Arrival time: _____________

    • End time: _____________

    • Where to meet: _____________

    • What to wear: Comfortable clothes that can get messy

    • What to bring: Just yourself! (We provide materials)

    Check with the Teacher¶

    • What is today's activity?

    • What grade level?

    • Which access/safety instructions are necessary for my assigned role?

    • Where should I be stationed?

    School Requirements¶

    • Signed volunteer form on file

    • Required screening/safeguarding confirmed with school (exact Archdiocesan policy: VERIFICATION REQUIRED)

    • Sign in at the office

    ⏱️ Typical C-STREAM Session¶

    Time What's Happening Your Role
    Opening (2-3 min) Prayer, wonder question Participate, model reverence
    Introduction (5-10 min) Teacher explains activity Listen, prepare materials
    Hands-On Time (15-25 min) Students build/create/explore Circulate, assist, encourage
    Sharing (3-5 min) Students share work Listen, celebrate
    Closing (2 min) Cleanup, closing prayer Help with cleanup

    💬 How to Talk to Students¶

    Instead of... Try...¶

    Instead of... Try...
    "That's wrong" "Tell me about your design"
    "Do it this way" "What happens if you try...?"
    "That won't work" "Interesting! What do you think will happen?"
    "Let me fix it" "What could you change?"
    "Good job!" "I noticed you tried 3 different ways—that's perseverance!"

    Great Questions to Ask¶

    To spark thinking:

    • "What are you trying to make?"

    • "What's your plan?"

    • "What do you think will happen?"

    When they're stuck:

    • "What have you tried so far?"

    • "What could you try next?"

    • "Who could you ask for ideas?"

    After testing:

    • "What happened?"

    • "What worked well?"

    • "What would you change?"

    Faith connections:

    • "What does this teach you about God's creation?"

    • "How could this help someone?"

    • "What are you grateful for in this project?"

    🔧 Common Volunteer Tasks¶

    Before Class¶

    • Set out materials at stations

    • Count supplies (enough for each group)

    • Test technology if applicable (iPads charged, apps open)

    • Prepare any teacher-requested materials

    During Class¶

    • Circulate among groups

    • Distribute additional supplies as needed

    • Help with technology issues (basic troubleshooting)

    • Encourage struggling students

    • Redirect off-task behavior gently ("What's your next step?")

    • Take photos if requested (check photo policy first!)

    After Class¶

    • Help students clean up their areas

    • Sort and organize materials

    • Count/inventory supplies

    • Wipe down tables if needed

    • Debrief with teacher (What went well? Any concerns?)

    🛠️ Working with Different Ages¶

    Kindergarten (25-minute sessions)¶

    • Need lots of support — Stay close, help with fine motor tasks

    • Short attention spans — Keep them focused on one step at a time

    • Encourage exploration — Mistakes inform learning; observe the specific concept and safety rules

    • Celebrate everything — "Look what you made!"

    Grades 1-2 (30-minute sessions)¶

    • Building independence — Let them try before helping

    • Reading support — They may need instructions read aloud

    • Partner work — Help them collaborate nicely

    • Encourage iteration — "What if you tried it again?"

    Grades 3-4 (40-minute sessions)¶

    • More independent — Step back, observe, intervene less

    • Group dynamics — Help ensure everyone participates

    • Deeper questions — Push their thinking with "why" and "how"

    • Documentation — May need help recording their process

    Grades 5-6 (45-minute sessions)¶

    • Very independent — Your role is mostly material support

    • Complex projects — Ask about their design thinking

    • Leadership opportunities — Can they help others?

    • Critical thinking — Challenge them to go deeper

    🚨 What to Do When...¶

    A student is frustrated¶

    1. Acknowledge feelings: "This is tricky, isn't it?"
    2. Normalize struggle: "Real engineers face problems too!"
    3. Focus on process: "What have you tried?"
    4. Suggest a break: "Take a breath, then look again"
    5. Celebrate effort: "I see you're not giving up!"

    A project "fails"¶

    1. Reframe it: "That's data! Now you know what doesn't work."
    2. Connect to learning: "What did you learn from this?"
    3. Encourage iteration: "How could you change it?"
    4. Share stories: "Even famous inventors failed many times!"

    Students are arguing¶

    1. Stay neutral: "What's the disagreement about?"
    2. Facilitate: "Can you each share your idea?"
    3. Problem-solve: "Is there a way to try both?"
    4. Involve teacher if needed

    You don't know the answer¶

    1. Be honest: "Great question! I'm not sure."
    2. Model learning: "Let's think about this together."
    3. Ask the student: "What do YOU think?"
    4. Check with teacher if needed

    A student is off-task¶

    1. Redirect gently: "What step are you on?"
    2. Give a job: "Can you be the materials manager?"
    3. Move closer: Sometimes proximity is enough
    4. Involve teacher for persistent issues

    Technology doesn't work¶

    1. Basic troubleshooting: Restart app, check connections
    2. Use the teacher's named backup; paper algorithms do not demonstrate real programming/robot execution
    3. Pair students: Share working devices
    4. Stay calm: Tech problems happen to everyone

    ✝️ Faith Integration Tips¶

    C-STREAM isn't just STEM—it's Catholic STEM! Help students make faith connections:

    Simple Connections¶

    • "Isn't it amazing that God created all of this?"

    • "How does this show God's love for us?"

    • "Engineers help people—just like we're called to do!"

    • "What can this teach us about being patient like God is with us?"

    When Students Struggle¶

    • "God doesn't give up on us, and we don't give up on our projects!"

    • "Making mistakes is part of how God helps us learn."

    • "Let's ask God to help us figure this out."

    During Teamwork¶

    • "How are we showing kindness to our teammates?"

    • "Jesus worked with a team too—his disciples!"

    • "Using our talents together is how we serve God."

    Print and keep with you! ✂️¶

    C-STREAM VOLUNTEER QUICK GUIDE

    DO:

    • Ask questions, don't give answers

    • Encourage every attempt

    • Let them struggle a little (productive struggle!)

    • Celebrate effort, not just success

    • Connect to faith when natural

    SAY:

    • "Tell me about your design"

    • "What could you try next?"

    • "That's great problem-solving!"

    • "How does this help us appreciate God's creation?"

    WHEN STUCK:

    • "What have you tried?"

    • "What's one thing you could change?"

    • "Can you ask a classmate?"

    REMEMBER:

    • It's okay not to know the answer

    • "Failure" is learning

    • Process matters more than product

    • You're modeling curiosity!

    ❓ Frequently Asked Questions¶

    Q: What if I'm not good at science/technology?
    A: That's okay! You're here to support and encourage, not teach. Your enthusiasm matters more than expertise.

    Q: Can I help my own child's class?
    A: Usually yes! Check with the teacher about classroom policies.

    Q: What if a student says something about faith I don't know how to answer?
    A: It's fine to say, "That's a great question! Let's ask [teacher] or you could ask your parents."

    Q: Should I post photos on social media?
    A: Please don't post photos of students without explicit school permission. Many families have privacy concerns.

    Q: How often should I volunteer?
    A: Whatever works for you! Weekly, monthly, or special events—all help is appreciated.

    Q: What if I can't make my scheduled time?
    A: Let the teacher know as soon as possible so they can adjust plans.

    Before serving:

    Lord, thank You for the opportunity to serve these children. Help me encourage their curiosity, celebrate their efforts, and point them toward You in all they learn. Give me patience when things are challenging and joy in their discoveries. Amen.

    🙏 Liturgical Prayers for STREAM¶

    Opening Prayer (General)¶

    "Loving God, You created all things with wisdom and love. Open our minds to discover the wonders of Your creation. Help us use what we learn to serve others and give You glory. Amen."

    Advent STREAM Prayer¶

    "Lord Jesus, Light of the World, as we wait for Your coming, help us see Your presence in all we learn and create. May our work bring hope to others. Amen."

    Lenten STREAM Prayer¶

    "Merciful God, as we journey toward Easter, help us use our gifts to serve those in need. May we build with simplicity, create with purpose, and share with generosity. Amen."

    Easter STREAM Prayer¶

    "Risen Lord, You make all things new! As we explore Your creation, fill us with the joy of Easter. Help us see new life and new possibilities in everything we do. Alleluia! Amen."

    End-of-Year STREAM Prayer¶

    "Holy Spirit, thank You for the gifts of wonder, creativity, and learning. As we finish this year, help us carry what we've learned into the world, serving others with the talents You've given us. Amen."

    Budget and supply request templates¶

    Use the single Materials Plan and Inventory CSV; do not reuse the earlier inconsistent annual estimates, fixed loan claims or donor price promises. All costs are October 2026 planning estimates, NOT vendor quotations.

    Administration request (copy and complete)¶

    Date / to / from / school year: [ ]

    We request [configuration] for [number of cohorts] with capacity [up to 25 students per class]. The low-tech core supports individual observation, measurement, investigation, design/redesign, unplugged computing and authentic arts/music. Catholic identity informs dignity, truth, service and stewardship.

    Cost category Amount Evidence/assumption
    Goods, including first-year consumables [ ] Attach selected bill of materials
    Tax reserve [ ] 8% planning assumption; actual rate/exemption VERIFICATION REQUIRED
    Shipping reserve [ ] Confirm supplier/delivery
    Annual durable-replacement reserve [ ] Inspect equipment condition
    Total requested [sum] Below chosen ceiling; do not force spending
    Estimated recurring year-two total [ ] Separate from first-year total, using plan's cohort basis

    Conditional existing inventory: [Physical count/date/location and missing basics.] What is not covered: [All legacy lessons, specialty loans/apps, personal devices, simultaneous classrooms, extra cohorts unless costed.] Evaluation: [One named objective, individual prompt and evidence threshold; not unsupported achievement or recruitment promises.] Procurement/source questions: [Supplier specification/availability, electrical protection, ingredients, school privacy/license approval; VERIFICATION REQUIRED.]

    The school funds all required materials and work time. Donations and loans are optional enhancements, not prerequisites. Official Minnesota/Archdiocesan/NCEA alignment is claimed only after source verification.

    Grant / donor / optional donation copy¶

    Grant summary: "We seek [amount] for [specific materials/objectives/cohorts]. We will document [individual evidence] and inspect/replenish kits annually." Do not invent baseline results, grant eligibility or official accreditation.

    Optional donation: "Clean, dry flat cardboard is welcome after teacher screening. Donating is optional; every child has school-provided supplies. Please send no batteries, magnets, glass, sharp metal, latex or chemical/food-soiled containers." No suggested dollar level promises a month/semester of lessons.

    Thank-you: "Thank you for [confirmed contribution]. It supported [actual learning/material use]." Photographs require verified consent. Tax deductibility, school legal status, gift-processing arrangements and monetary donation instructions are VERIFICATION REQUIRED with administration.

    STREAM Night & Family Event Guide¶

    {: .no_toc }

    Table of Contents¶

    {: .no_toc .text-delta }

    1. TOC

    Overview¶

    STREAM Night is a celebration of student learning that brings families together to experience hands-on Science, Technology, Religion, Engineering, Art, and Math activities. This guide provides everything you need to plan a successful STREAM Night or family showcase event at Our Lady of the Prairie Catholic School.

    October 2026 operating conditions: C is Catholic identity, R is explicit religion/faith integration, A includes arts/music, and M is mathematics. This optional event celebrates in-school learning; no home-built project, purchased display board, family attendance or donation affects grades. Use the family copy system and objective-linked rubric. Event costs below are separate planning estimates, not vendor quotes or part of the core classroom budgets. Re-cost for actual attendance, tax and shipping. Confirm staffing, venue capacity, accommodations, safeguarding and photo/consent procedures with the school. Scripture quotations and Church attributions below are VERIFICATION REQUIRED before printing; devotional symbolism is not scientific evidence.

    SAFETY: No button cells, latex balloons or projectile stations; no neodymium magnets in K. Adults manage electrical power, small parts and safe bounded tests. Close unstaffed hazardous stations rather than assuming volunteers will arrive. Plan an indoor January version and accessible seated/silent routes. Suspected battery/magnet ingestion or other urgent danger triggers immediate school emergency escalation. Use counted kits.

    Why Host a STREAM Night?¶

    Benefit Description
    Family Engagement Parents experience what their children learn
    Student Pride Children showcase their work and explain their thinking
    Community Building Strengthens school-family-parish connections
    Faith Integration Demonstrates how faith and reason work together
    STEM Excitement Generates enthusiasm for STEM learning
    Recruitment Attracts prospective families to your school

    Event Format Options¶

    Option 1: Student Showcase (Recommended for First Event)¶

    Duration: 90 minutes
    Best For: Displaying student work from throughout the year

    Structure:

    • Students stand by their projects

    • Families rotate through displays

    • Students explain their work to visitors

    • Interactive elements at each station

    Option 2: Interactive STREAM Stations¶

    Duration: 2 hours
    Best For: Hands-on family experiences

    Structure:

    • 6-8 activity stations around the space

    • Families rotate every 15-20 minutes

    • Each station has a hands-on challenge

    • Volunteers facilitate each station

    Option 3: STREAM Fair (Competition Format)¶

    Duration: 3 hours
    Best For: Older students (grades 3-6)

    Structure:

    • Students complete assessed work during school; optional home conversation only

    • Projects displayed using school paper/models; purchased boards not required

    • Judges evaluate using rubrics

    • Awards ceremony at conclusion

    Option 4: Family Engineering Night¶

    Duration: 90 minutes
    Best For: Maximum participation

    Structure:

    • Families work together on challenges

    • All families do the same activity simultaneously

    • Emphasis on teamwork and fun

    • Simple, no-pressure format

    Planning Timeline¶

    Week 8 Tasks:

    • Choose event date (check parish/school calendar)

    • Select event format

    • Reserve venue (gym, cafeteria, parish hall)

    • Set budget with administration

    • Begin promoting to families

    Committee Roles: | Role | Responsibilities | |------|------------------| | Event Coordinator | Overall planning, communication | | Volunteer Coordinator | Recruit and train helpers | | Setup/Cleanup Lead | Room arrangement, teardown | | Materials Manager | Gather and organize supplies | | Technology Support | Projector, music, slideshow | | Hospitality Lead | Refreshments, welcome table |

    Activity Station Ideas¶

    Station 1: Tower Building Challenge¶

    Faith Connection: Building our faith on a strong foundation

    Item Details
    Materials Large blocks, folded paper or dry cups; no food prerequisite
    Challenge Build the tallest tower in 10 minutes
    Scripture "Built on the rock" (Matthew 7:24-27)
    Volunteer Needed Yes - 1 facilitator

    Station 2: Coding Corner¶

    Faith Connection: God gave us creativity and problem-solving minds

    Item Details
    Materials Preapproved tested devices only if confirmed; large arrow cards and desk grids for a separate unplugged concept activity
    Challenge Complete a coding puzzle or program a robot
    Scripture "For we are God's handiwork" (Ephesians 2:10)
    Volunteer Needed Yes - 1-2 helpers

    Station 3: Tabletop Simple Machines¶

    Faith Connection: Using knowledge responsibly to help others

    Item Details
    Materials Enclosed classroom pulley, short cord, light teacher-controlled desk-level load
    Challenge Compare how the pulley changes the direction of a gentle pull; no launching or overhead loads
    Source status Faith-source wording VERIFICATION REQUIRED; no forced Scripture analogy
    Volunteer Needed Yes - 1 facilitator

    Station 4: Bridge Building¶

    Faith Connection: Building bridges to serve others

    Item Details
    Materials Paper/cardboard, rulers, stable supports, ten index cards per team for controlled tests
    Challenge Compare two bridge forms using the same gap and counted cards; no uncontrolled heavy weights
    Scripture "Bear one another's burdens" (Galatians 6:2)
    Volunteer Needed Yes - 1 facilitator

    Station 5: Art & Math Symmetry¶

    Faith Connection: Finding God's patterns in creation

    Item Details
    Materials Graph paper, colored pencils, symmetry cards
    Challenge Create symmetrical designs
    Scripture "He has made everything beautiful" (Ecclesiastes 3:11)
    Volunteer Needed Optional

    Station 6: Science Discovery¶

    Faith Connection: Exploring God's wonderful creation

    Item Details
    Materials Magnifying glasses, nature items, microscopes
    Challenge Observe and draw what you discover
    Scripture "The heavens declare the glory of God" (Psalm 19:1)
    Volunteer Needed Yes - 1 facilitator

    Station 7: Circuit Creations¶

    Faith Connection: Being a light to the world

    Item Details
    Materials Verified protected switched 2-AA packs, current-limited 3-V LED modules and insulated leads; adult-managed cells
    Challenge Complete a circuit to light up an LED
    Scripture "You are the light of the world" (Matthew 5:14)
    Volunteer Needed Yes - 1 helper

    Station 8: Prayer & Reflection¶

    Faith Connection: Center of our STREAM learning

    Item Details
    Materials Prayer cards, journals, quiet seating
    Activity Write a prayer of thanks for God's creation
    Scripture Various creation and wonder verses
    Volunteer Needed Optional

    Faith Integration Ideas¶

    Opening Prayer¶

    Creator God,

    Thank you for the gift of wonder and curiosity. Thank you for the minds You have given us to explore Your creation.

    Tonight, we celebrate learning together as a community. Help us see Your hand in science, technology, engineering, art, and math.

    Bless our families as they discover and create together. May everything we learn draw us closer to You.

    We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

    Closing Prayer¶

    Loving God,

    Thank you for this time together as a school family. We are grateful for our students and all they have learned. We are grateful for our teachers who guide them with faith and love. We are grateful for families who support learning at home.

    As we go home tonight, help us continue to wonder, to question, and to discover. May we use our talents to serve others and glorify You.

    We ask this in Jesus' name. Amen.

    Volunteer Information¶

    Volunteer Briefing Script¶

    Read to volunteers before event:

    "Thank you for helping with STREAM Night! Here are a few things to remember:

    1. Be welcoming - Smile and greet every family
    2. Encourage participation - Offer accessible choices and confirmed station capacity; do not require every activity
    3. Let kids lead - Guide, don't take over
    4. Keep it positive - There's no wrong way to explore
    5. Connect to faith - Use the scripture signs as conversation starters
    6. Watch the clock - Help families move when it's time
    7. Have fun! - Your enthusiasm is contagious

    Questions? Find me (Event Coordinator) in the _____ area."

    Troubleshooting Common Issues¶

    Low Registration Numbers¶

    Solutions:

    • Send personal reminders

    • Have students invite grandparents

    • Partner with parish events

    • Offer incentives (raffle prize for attendees)

    • Simplify the event to reduce intimidation

    Not Enough Volunteers¶

    Solutions:

    • Reduce number of stations

    • Ask 8th graders or Confirmation students to help

    • Partner with Knights of Columbus or other parish groups

    • Have teachers facilitate instead of parents

    Running Out of Supplies¶

    Solutions:

    • Have backup simple activities ready

    • Set limits per family at each station

    • Cross-train floaters to help manage supplies

    • Focus on reusable materials

    Crowd Management¶

    Solutions:

    • Use timed rotations with a bell/announcement

    • Assign families to starting stations

    • Have clear directional signs

    • Position greeters at each area

    Technology Issues¶

    Solutions:

    • Test everything day before

    • Have paper backups for coding activities

    • Bring extra batteries

    • Ensure good WiFi or offline alternatives

    After the Event¶

    Thank You Notes¶

    Send within one week:

    • Thank volunteers personally

    • Send note home to all families

    • Thank administration and parish support

    • Acknowledge any sponsors

    Documentation¶

    • Collect photos from volunteers/families

    • Write brief summary for newsletter

    • Note what worked well

    • Note what to improve

    • Save materials list for next year

    • Store reusable supplies properly

    Evaluation Questions¶

    Ask Planning Committee: 1. What went really well? 2. What would we do differently? 3. Did families seem engaged? 4. Were there any safety concerns? 5. Was the timeline appropriate? 6. What feedback did you hear from families?

    Templates

    C-STREAM templates¶

    October 2026 formats for K-6; complete bracketed fields before teaching. Native periods: K 25, grades 1-2 30, grades 3-4 40, grades 5-6 45 minutes.

    C is Catholic identity; R is religion/faith integration; A is arts including music; M is mathematics. Art includes observation, composition, design, performance and communication without a screen; it is not merely decoration. Only claim domains genuinely practiced. All required work and supplies are provided at school; no routine homework or donation prerequisites.

    Creating... Use What it protects
    One meeting Lesson plan At a glance, background/vocabulary, native timings, safety, scaling and individual evidence
    A unit Cross-curricular unit Prerequisites, meeting sequence, balance, logistics, family copy
    Multi-meeting project PBL overlay Launch/research/create/present using the same unit and lesson formats
    Student response Student sheet Show/tell/draw or record; nonreader route
    Substitute handoff Substitute lesson 20-minute preparation gate and named fallbacks
    Individual evidence Assessment Objective -> prompt -> success condition -> student evidence
    ¾-level criteria Rubric Observable objective-linked levels, not participation or polish
    Family copy Newsletter Actual learning and optional no-purchase conversation/activity
    Materials/kit Materials list Normalized items, 10/15/20/25 quantities and replenishment
    Standards evidence Standards mapping Local catalog and separately verified official alignment

    The local 18-code catalog defines CST-C1..C3, CST-S1..S3, CST-T1..T3, CST-E1..E3, CST-A1..A3 and CST-M1..M3. Do not generate new local codes or label these official Archdiocesan/Minnesota standards. Official source questions remain VERIFICATION REQUIRED.

    Operational entry points: materials, technology, substitutes, family communication, rubrics, student resources.

    C-STREAM lesson plan template¶

    Version 3.0 - October 2026. Copy and complete this format; bracketed fields are author prompts, not finished instructions. Preserve a useful existing lesson, its URL and learning purpose when bringing it into this format.

    C = Catholic identity; S = science; T = technology (tools and computing); R = religion/faith integration; E = engineering; A = arts, including visual art, design and music; M = mathematics, not music. Catholic identity informs purpose, dignity, truth and stewardship throughout. R names the explicit faith teaching/reflection. Art must involve an artistic decision, observation, composition or communication, not simply decorating a STEM product. Emphasize only domains students actually practice; do not claim all seven in every lesson.

    Lesson at a glance¶

    Field Complete before teaching
    Grade; rotation; schedule; unit; title [K/½/¾/⅚; A/B; weekly/bi-weekly; unit; title]
    Time [K 25 / grades 1-2 30 / grades 3-4 40 / grades 5-6 45 minutes]
    Big idea; why learn this? [Concept and everyday/service/vocation application]
    Learning objective O1 "I can [observable action + concept + success condition]."
    Optional O2 [Second objective only if teachable and assessable in this period]
    C-STREAM areas addressed [C/S/T/R/E/A/M and actual student action for each claimed domain]
    Catholic connection [A concrete design/ethical/stewardship decision; not prayer alone]
    Faith source/status [Primary-source URL, section, paraphrase/quotation status; VERIFICATION REQUIRED if unresolved]

    Exact lesson sequence¶

    The following allocations total the native period and protect test/redesign, individual evidence and cleanup. Choose ONE column; replace actions with exact directions and materials. Do not add untimed prayer, transitions or worksheets.

    Step K: 25 1-2: 30 3-4: 40 5-6: 45 Teacher says/does; student action
    1. Hook, purpose, Catholic connection 0-3 0-3 0-4 0-4 "[Actual question]"; [brief prayer if appropriate]
    2. Vocabulary, model and safety 3-7 3-8 4-10 4-11 [Demonstrate one complete action; ask a check question]
    3. Plan and build/investigate 7-14 8-18 10-24 11-27 [Numbered, concrete directions; rotate builder/tester/reporter]
    4. Test, compare and improve 14-19 18-23 24-32 27-36 [Same test conditions; one evidence-based change and retest]
    5. Individual objective-linked check 19-22 23-27 32-37 36-41 [Each child shows/tells/draws O1; record evidence]
    6. Cleanup and close 22-25 27-30 37-40 41-45 [Count, sort, disconnect, dry and return; closing thought]

    Questions to ask: "[What changed?]"; "[What stayed the same?]"; "[What evidence supports your choice?]"; "[Who does this design include?]"; "[How did you avoid waste?]" Supply topic-specific versions, not just "facilitate discussion."

    K-1/nonreader directions: [Show the real object, say ONE step, let students do it, repeat. Use pointing, sorting, building, gesture and dictated evidence.]

    What success looks like / individual assessment¶

    Objective Individual prompt/task Meets expectation Evidence/mode Local code
    O1 [Actual exit question/demo] [Observable threshold] [Teacher roster: each child's response, not team product alone] [ ]
    O2 if taught [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Use assessment and rubric formats. Levels: 1 Beginning, 2 Developing, 3 Meets Expectation, 4 Extends Learning; NE = not yet evidenced, not a zero. Participation, handwriting, neatness, confidence and artistic talent are not proxies for O1. Score an arts criterion only when that arts skill is an explicit objective.

    At 25 students, gather a quick simultaneous point/show/draw response and use a planned roster sweep during hands-on time. If oral conferences need more time, record NE and schedule a check next meeting; never claim all were assessed. At expected-mastery checkpoints, Local Standards requires two dated observations on separate occasions with an individual demonstration and changed context/follow-up explanation. One exit check alone does not establish end-of-grade mastery.

    Support and challenge¶

    Support: [Read aloud; fewer choices; pre-cut pieces; larger tools; bilingual vocabulary/gesture; seated/quiet option; adult scribing. Keep the same concept unless explicitly documenting an objective change.]

    Challenge: [Add a justified constraint, repeat trial, compare data, or explain a tradeoff. Do not routinely turn faster learners into helpers.]

    Use only the local catalog: CST-C1/C2/C3, CST-S1/S2/S3, CST-T1/T2/T3, CST-E1/E2/E3, CST-A1/A2/A3, CST-M1/M2/M3. Definitions and grade expectations belong to Local Standards, not this template.     Project-based learning template¶

    Use the unit template as the planning record and lesson template for each meeting. This project overlay preserves Launch -> Research -> Create -> Present without creating a competing lesson format. Version 3.0 - October 2026.

    • Technology Requirement: [None / Optional / Recommended / Required, per meeting; why and what changes without it.]

    Phase Linked native-period meeting(s) Student work Individual evidence/checkpoint

    Criteria, responsibilities and access¶

    Success criteria: [Measurable conditions, not "beautiful," "creative" or "participates well."] Constraints: [Time, materials, safety, cost.] Team roles/rotation: [Builder/tester/reporter; each child gets a hands-on turn.] Individual deliverable: [Show/tell/draw/record; use the student sheet or nonreader card rather than a mandatory written report.] Arts objective if used: [Composition, pattern, observation, musical phrase or visual communication; assess the named skill rather than expensive presentation.]

    Complete the unit's materials/safety/support/challenge/fallback sections, including 10/15/20/25 scaling, teacher-only prep, exact test and cleanup. Retain records between meetings in labeled bins; no fragile work transported home as a requirement. School supplies and work time cover participation.

    Catholic purpose and service¶

    • Who might benefit? [An authentic, respectfully described user need.]
    • Which decision honors dignity or care for creation? [Actual example.]
    • Faith source: [Primary URL/section; VERIFICATION REQUIRED if unverified.]
    • Classroom model vs actual service: [Do not claim a prototype has helped people without evidence. Do not deploy assistive/medical/structural devices or drinking-water filters without qualified adult review.]
    • Optional visitors, parish partnerships and events need confirmation and a school-run alternative; they are not prerequisites.

    Assessment and family copy¶

    Use the assessment template and student project rubric. Share 1-3 objective-linked criteria before launch. No universal 100-point or faith/ presentation weighting. Technical evidence and faith reasoning remain distinguishable; neither team success nor enthusiasm proves individual mastery.

    Use the newsletter template at launch and completion. No routine homework, home research, donation, purchased board, family attendance or personal device required. Optional no-purchase family conversation: "[One actual question a child can answer orally.]"

    Before reuse¶

    Record observed prep/cleanup minutes, consumables per cohort, individual evidence still missing, unsafe/missing parts, verified sources, objective changes and revisions. Use Standards Mapping to connect only practiced standards from Local Standards.

    Example, not an official grade benchmark: O1 compare two paper structures under the same load. Prompt: "Show which held the load, and what stayed the same in your test." Meets: identifies the observed result and keeps span/load placement the same. A failed bridge can supply valid evidence.

    Use Rubric Template. NE means not yet evidenced; absence, missed observation or equipment failure does not prove low mastery. Ordinary access accommodations do not cap a score. Distinguish a conceptual hint from read-aloud, translation, scribing or motor assistance.

    Collect a response from every child; a group prototype is supporting evidence, not an individual score. At 25, observe nine teams during hands-on work plus simultaneous exit responses. Mark any unobserved child NE and arrange a brief next-meeting check. Give one specific feedback statement and one next action. Do not average unrelated objectives or replace learning evidence with participation, prayer behavior, confidence or attractive displays.

    Expected-mastery checkpoints: Follow Local Standards: at least two dated observations on separate occasions, including an individually attributable demonstration and a changed context or follow-up explanation; both meet the grade target. A single lesson's level 3 is that occasion's evidence, not end-of-grade mastery. Record NE/not yet assessed when evidence is missing and schedule the next check.

    Device objective: [Record actual program execution/robot action if required. Paper algorithm evidence does not establish programming mastery.] Faith objective if assessed: [Reasoned choice/understanding of taught content, not strength of belief, prayer frequency or family practice.] Official alignment: [Verified URL/version/benchmark or VERIFICATION REQUIRED.]

    Objective-linked rubric template¶

    Grade/unit/lesson: [ ] Objective/code: [ ] Prompt: [ ] Modes/support: [Show/tell/draw/record, read-aloud/scribe/larger materials.] Select 1-3 criteria genuinely taught. State the Meets condition first.

    Criterion linked to objective 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning (optional)
    [Observable concept/action] [Evidence reveals named misconception or missing action] [Partial evidence; specify missing part] [Exact success condition] [Transfers/explains using additional evidence; not beyond-grade content by default]

    For a three-level rubric omit column 4; do not relabel NE as Beginning. NE: not yet evidenced sits outside the scale.

    Completed example¶

    O1: Compare flat and folded paper using an equal span and load.

    Criterion 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning
    Evidence-based comparison Names a result different from the observed test Names the observed stronger design but cannot identify the common test condition yet Names the observed result and shows equal span and load placement Repeats the fair test and explains whether the second result supports the first

    A collapsed bridge can still meet this objective. Decorative skill, participation, handwriting, family help and confident speech are not this criterion. If the objective is a rhythmic pattern or visual composition, write a separate arts criterion measuring that named artistic decision, not "looks beautiful." Assess Catholic reasoning from taught content, not a child's interior faith.

    Scoring/evidence record: use Assessment Template. One Meets rating is evidence for that occasion. Expected-mastery checkpoints require two dated observations on separate occasions under Local Standards, not one polished project. Source/status: local teacher criterion; official standards alignment requires verification in Standards Mapping.
