    Rubrics

    C-STREAM rubrics¶

    October 2026 revision: lightweight ¾-level evidence rather than universal 100-point weighting. State the objective, prompt and Meets condition first. NE = not yet evidenced, not a zero or proof of low mastery.

    Need Resource Audience
    Project science/design/math/arts evidence Student project rubric Teacher/student; each child demonstrates learning
    Reasoning, communication or taught collaboration skill Skills assessment Teacher; observable actions, not personality
    Taught dignity/service/stewardship reasoning Service rubric Teacher/student; no compulsory external service
    Quality/accuracy of faith integration in a lesson Faith-reason rubric Teacher/administrator; NOT a student belief score
    Write a specific criterion Rubric template Lesson author; three or four levels
    Record each child's evidence Assessment template Teacher; prompt, evidence, feedback, next check

    Assessment measures the stated objective, not participation, handwriting, neatness, presentation expense or confidence. An arts criterion assesses a named composition/design/performance skill only if taught as an objective. Accept show/tell/draw/scribe/record with access supports. Failed models can provide excellent evidence; a working group product does not establish every child's mastery. Never grade prayer habits, family religion or interior belief.

    Use the 18 local codes with actual lesson evidence. Official standards/Church quotation claims require source verification. Do not equate a rubric score with complete official curriculum alignment.

    Faith-reason integration lesson-quality rubric¶

    Audience: teachers/administrators, not a student faith score. October 2026. Preserves the earlier focus on faith/reason, Catholic teaching, wonder, heritage and service while avoiding a compulsory saint/Scripture/prayer formula for every lesson. C shapes the purpose and choices; R is explicit faith teaching/reflection. Scientific inquiry remains evidence-based.

    Local planning criteria¶

    Lesson-quality criterion 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Quality
    Faith and empirical reasoning distinguished Religious claim presented as experimental proof, or science misstated Connection named but distinction unclear Scientifically accurate evidence and Catholic reflection distinguished Teacher background anticipates a misconception and models a careful source/evidence response
    Catholic purpose affects work No connection or prayer alone General value named without a classroom decision Students consider a specific dignity, stewardship, truth or service choice Choice is revisited using results, user needs or a tradeoff
    Source accuracy Invented/misattributed standard, quotation or Church claim Source question marked but not yet resolved Primary source checked, quoted/paraphrased accurately and linked Appropriate context and limits are explained in teacher-friendly language
    Inquiry and wonder Questions suppressed or inquiry replaced by a craft Wonder question named but no student investigation Students observe/ask/test and reflect without forced theological inference New student questions guide a feasible next investigation
    Access and evidence Participation/prayer behavior graded as belief Flexible modes named but criteria unclear Named objective assessed with individual oral/drawn/model/written evidence Results inform specific access support and next teaching

    Mark optional heritage/service extensions N/A if not relevant to that lesson; do not add points for more quotations, longer prayers or named scientists. Record dimension evidence, not a /20 total suggesting official certification. Unresolved source accuracy is a readiness blocker, not a minor score offset.

    Source pathway: Local Standards and the shared review's authoritative source record. A primary reference for faith/reason is Fides et Ratio. VERIFICATION REQUIRED for exact passage/quotation and any claimed diocesan or state requirement. This rubric is local, not an official Church standard.

    Lesson review record¶

    Lesson/date/reviewer Criterion Evidence/link Level/N/A Revision/source question
    [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Useful prompts: "Which design choice respects the person using this?" "What did our test show?" "How can we avoid waste?" "What remains unknown?" Avoid "God is an engineer" as an explanatory scientific analogy. Historical biographies, devotional comparisons and scientific evidence require different source handling; consult background guides critically, not as proof.

    If assessing a student Catholic objective, use the student project rubric for taught reasoning. Never grade interior belief, awe, prayer frequency or family religious practice.

    Service-oriented STEM rubric¶

    Select this when the lesson explicitly teaches a reasoned design/service decision. Do not require every science investigation to be a deployed service project. October 2026. C is Catholic identity; R is the explicit faith teaching/reflection. A classroom prototype is not evidence of real-world impact.

    Source and age conditions¶

    Use the local Catholic standards and the verified source record. A primary source for the social-teaching themes is the USCCB themes overview. VERIFICATION REQUIRED for exact lesson paraphrases/quotations, source sections, diocesan requirements and current approval. This is a local classroom rubric, not an official USCCB/Archdiocesan scoring instrument.

    Keep beneficiaries respectfully described. Do not simulate disability, use real student medical profiles or deploy medical/assistive/structural/water-purification prototypes without qualified adult review. Ordinary academic inquiry and individual work are not less valuable or less Catholic than group outreach.

    Explicit objective/criterion 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning
    Identify a user need Names a solution without a relevant need Names user/need but link is incomplete Names a concrete user need and shows how a design choice responds Compares two choices using user constraints/feedback
    Apply taught dignity/service principle Proposed choice conflicts with the taught concern Names the principle but cannot yet connect the choice Explains how one choice respects the taught principle Explains a tradeoff and a way to address an unintended exclusion
    Explain stewardship Does not yet identify a resource consequence Names a resource but not the effect of the choice Explains a specific reuse/waste choice and consequence Compares alternatives using material/cost or test evidence
    Distinguish prototype from impact Claims a model has solved a real problem without evidence Recognizes it is a model but cannot state the limit Explains what was tested and what remains unproven for real use Suggests a safe next test or appropriate adult consultation

    Use only selected objectives. Fill in the exact grade-appropriate success condition; K can point to a saved material and explain whom a design helps. Grades 5-6 can reason about two alternatives and limitations. NE sits outside the scale. Access accommodations do not lower scores.

    Individual evidence and reflection¶

    Child Objective/code Actual explanation/choice Mode/support Level/NE Feedback
    [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Ask: "Who might use it?" "What need are you addressing?" "What did the test actually show?" "Which choice avoids waste?" "Who could be left out?" Assess understanding of taught content, not motivation, charitable donations, family resources, prayer practice or interior belief.

    Service possibilities preserved from the earlier guide: classroom models of accessible tools, stewardship systems, environmental observations and helpful information designs. Partners and actual deployment are optional confirmed extensions, never prerequisites to classroom mastery.

    Thinking, communication and collaboration assessment¶

    The earlier question banks on reasoning, communication, collaboration, creativity, curiosity and ethics remain useful purposes. Select an explicitly taught objective, not a universal character score. October 2026.

    Taught objective 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning
    Justify a design choice with evidence Choice contradicts observed evidence Gives a relevant choice but evidence link is incomplete Explains the choice with the specified observed result Compares an alternative using another result or tradeoff
    Communicate a result Response does not yet convey the result Conveys part of the result Shows/tells/draws the result and relevant evidence clearly enough to interpret Adapts explanation after a clarifying question without changing the evidence
    Combine two ideas in a plan (only if an objective) Plan does not yet include either discussed idea Uses one idea, or includes both without explaining their use Identifies each idea and shows how they contribute to the plan Tests the combined plan and explains an improvement based on feedback
    Revise an artistic/design idea Change is unrelated to the purpose Relevant revision with an incomplete explanation Revises a taught visual/musical/design choice and explains its purpose Compares versions and explains an intentional effect or tradeoff
    Frame an investigable question Question cannot yet be investigated with the available evidence Question is relevant but too broad States a question answerable by the planned observation/test Refines it using results and identifies what to test next
    Explain a privacy/stewardship choice Does not yet recognize the taught concern Names the concern without linking the action Explains how a concrete choice addresses the taught concern Compares two actions and explains consequences for people/resources

    NE is not yet evidenced. Teacher read-aloud, bilingual response, gesture, scribe and motor assistance are access supports, not evidence of a lower level. Do not score smiles, spontaneous awe, public speaking confidence, written fluency, leadership, speed or active participation as subject mastery. Behavior/engagement can be noted separately for support planning without converting it into the objective's grade.

    Record and feedback¶

    Student/date Lesson/objective/local code Actual words/action Mode/support Level/NE Next prompt
    [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Use Assessment Template and Local Standards. Official alignment requires verification. No general /24 total or score for apparent strength of faith.

    Student/peer reflection (not a mastery grade)¶

    Read aloud if needed: "Show one idea you changed. What result made you change it?" / "Which idea did your partner contribute?" / "What will you test next?" Peers provide a specific appreciative statement and question, not star ratings of a child's personality. Teacher checks individual concept evidence separately.

    Student project rubric¶

    October 2026 revision. Replaces the universal 100-point weighting with a small selection of criteria matched to the taught objectives. Preserve science/ engineering, faith reasoning, service, communication and reflection as possible learning purposes, not compulsory scoring categories for every project.

    Before use¶

    1. Write grade/unit/lesson, objective O1/O2, individual prompt and success condition using Assessment Template.
    2. Select 1-3 relevant criteria below; adjust Meets to the lesson's exact measurable threshold and grade prerequisites before teaching.
    3. Link the defined local standard. Official alignment requires verification, not a claim that a score meets all standards.
    4. Share expectations by showing/telling students. Offer oral, model, drawing, scribed or written evidence. Team products support, but never replace, each child's demonstration.

    Four levels¶

    Objective-linked criterion (use only if taught) 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning
    O1 scientific observation/comparison Describes an outcome inconsistent with what was observed Names a relevant observation but comparison is incomplete Makes the specified comparison using an observed result Repeats or transfers the comparison and explains supporting evidence
    O1 fair test/engineering redesign Changes conditions without recognizing their effect Tests and suggests a change but evidence link is incomplete Uses the stated common conditions, records a result and justifies one redesign Retests the redesign and compares performance or a tradeoff using evidence
    O2 measurement/math reasoning Quantity/unit or comparison is incorrect Partly correct measure/data with a specific error remaining Measures/represents/explains using the lesson's specified quantity and unit Checks the result or uses it to justify a new comparison
    O2 algorithm/programming Sequence cannot produce intended result Sequence partly works; bug or execution evidence remains unresolved Explains/tests the intended sequence; real execution included if objective requires it Finds and tests a new correction/condition and explains the effect
    O2 artistic communication/music Chosen form/pattern does not yet convey the stated idea Artistic choice partly conveys the idea/phrase Uses the stated visual or musical choice to communicate the intended idea/phrase Revises a composition/phrase after feedback and explains the artistic effect
    O2 Catholic/ethical/service reasoning Choice does not yet address the taught dignity/stewardship principle Names the principle or user but connection to choice is incomplete Explains a concrete choice and how it respects the taught principle/user need Compares two choices and explains an evidence-informed tradeoff in light of the principle

    NE = not yet evidenced, outside the scale. Missed observation, absence, device failure or an inaccessible response mode is not Beginning. Access supports do not cap levels. A conceptual hint is recorded separately. Artistic skill is scored only for an explicit arts objective; handwriting, neatness, beautiful displays, expensive boards, confident speech, participation and family assistance are not mastery criteria. No grades for interior faith, prayer frequency, family religious practice or apparent enthusiasm.

    Individual score/evidence record¶

    Student Objective/local code Actual response/action Mode/access support Level or NE Feedback and next check
    [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Do not average unrelated objectives into a pseudo-precise total. Report "Compared two bridge tests using the same span; next, explain the redesign" instead of "earned 80%, meets all C-STREAM standards." Expected-mastery checkpoints follow Local Standards: two dated observations on separate occasions, including an individual demonstration and changed context/follow-up explanation, both meeting the target. One project rating does not establish end-of-grade mastery.

    Bridge example and moderation¶

    O1: Compare two paper designs under the same span/load conditions. Meets: child names the observed result and shows which conditions stayed the same. A failed prototype can provide successful learning evidence. A team's strong bridge with no individual explanation is NE for that child's comparison. Drawings can communicate the comparison without handwriting assessment.

    Before a showcase, two teachers score the same anonymized examples using the selected criteria and resolve discrepancies. Events are optional celebrations of in-school work; a child's assessment does not depend on home construction, family attendance or purchased display materials.

    Related: Rubric Template, faith lesson-quality rubric, service reasoning, thinking/communication.

    Student Resources

    Student resources¶

    Print only what the objective needs; a board-drawn prompt or oral response is equally valid. No reading/writing prerequisite for K-1. Adult models one step and accepts point/show/build/sort/tell/dictate; each child gets their own turn.

    Resource Purpose and use
    Show, Try, Tell Actual nonreader/adult-led comparison example and reusable response route
    Journal cover Optional personalized cover; black-and-white/hand-drawn works
    Goals Interest/next-learning conversation; not an achievement grade
    Engineering process Plan/test/improve evidence; select fields, not a mandatory long worksheet
    Wonder journal Questions/observations; enjoyment stars are not mastery
    Project reflection One objective/evidence prompt at a time; full reflection optional
    Student sheet template Teacher adapts objective, prompt, criterion and evidence mode

    Use assessment and rubrics for individual learning. Do not grade participation, handwriting, neatness or apparent faith as subject mastery. Arts skills are assessed only if explicit objectives; A includes music and M means mathematics. Named records follow the school's actual privacy practice. Local standard definitions: Local Standards; official alignment/source questions require verification.

    Show, Try, Tell¶

    Teacher/substitute: This is an adult-led card, not independent reading. Use it with the actual lesson objective and kit. A printed copy is optional. Draw the three boxes on the board or place three real objects as visual cues. Say ONE step, show it, let the child do it, then repeat. No homework.

    1. SHOW
    Adult points to the object.

    Child points, sorts or draws here.
    2. TRY
    Adult models one action.

    Child builds, tests or moves a large pointer.
    3. TELL
    Adult shows the result.

    Child points, gestures, tells or dictates.

    Ready-to-use comparison example (K/nonreader)¶

    Objective: "I can show which of two objects is longer." Materials: Two ordinary school pencils of visibly different lengths, each child's familiar drawing tool/paper optional. No small new parts or devices.

    1. Hold up the two pencils. Say "Look." Put them side by side with ends aligned.
    2. Model pointing along a pencil. Say "Show the longer one." Let each child point.
    3. Reverse left/right order, realign ends. Say "Show me again. How do you know?" Accept tracing, pointing at the unmatched end, gesture or words; adult scribes.

    Meets: Child identifies the longer pencil in both placements and indicates the unmatched end/aligned comparison. If position alone determines the answer, model aligned ends and recheck later. Do not score reading, handwriting or speech. This is a local classroom criterion, not a verified official benchmark.

    Support: Larger objects, extra wait time, adult holds objects steady, child uses gaze/gesture or home-language response. Challenge: Compare a third object and explain the order. Catholic connection: Care for shared tools and use them fairly; no scientific proof claim or forced comparison of God to an engineer. Safety: No sharpening/swinging; keep tools at desk level.

    Adapt to the planned lesson¶

    Teacher writes/reads objective [ ], actual question [ ], Meets condition [ ] and local code from Local Standards [ ]. Use real-object demonstration for build/test or large arrow cards for sequences. Keep each student's own turn; do not accept a partner's answer as their evidence.

    Child/date Exact action/words Objective Access support Level/NE Next check
    [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Use Assessment Template and Student Sheet for teacher records.

    About

    👋 About the Author¶

    Joe Vandermark¶

    With more than 30 years in technology, I'm passionate about helping people understand how computers, cloud systems, and new tools make life and work better. I created the C-STREAM Framework to bring that same spirit of innovation into Catholic education—nurturing both the mind and spirit.

    My Philosophy

    STREAM learning gives every student the confidence to explore, ask questions, and build the future with both skill and heart.

    💼 Professional Background¶

    Technology Leadership¶

    At Microsoft, I lead a team of Cloud Solution Architects who help companies build safe and creative solutions in the cloud. I've also authored two books on building strong, people-focused teams.

    Entrepreneurship & Wellness¶

    I'm a franchise owner and Chief Operating Officer for The Vital Stretch in the Twin Cities, where I'm building wellness studios that help people move better and stay healthy. I love connecting technology, business, wellness, and community in meaningful ways.

    Education & Service¶

    I volunteer as a STEM teacher at Our Lady of the Prairie Catholic School, where I help students discover how creativity, science, faith, and problem-solving work together. My background includes:

    ⛪ Faith & Service¶

    🤝 Contributing to C-STREAM

    Catholic Science, Technology, Religion, Engineering, Arts, and Math

    Thank you for your interest in contributing to the C-STREAM Framework! We welcome your input, whether it's submitting new lesson plans, improving existing resources, or helping us better integrate Catholic values into STEM education.

    Before editing curriculum, read the curriculum review, local standards and teaching-release priorities. Preserve baseline findings when recording a revision; a changed file is not automatically classroom-ready.

    📋 How to Contribute¶

    1. 🐛 Reporting Issues¶

    If you notice any issues with the framework, lesson plans, templates, or resources (e.g., broken links, typos, or inaccuracies), please help us by reporting them:

    1. Go to the Issues tab in the repository
    2. Click on New Issue
    3. Provide a clear description with as much detail as possible:
    4. The file where the issue exists
    5. What needs to be corrected
    6. Any suggested fixes

    2. 📝 Submitting New Lesson Plans¶

    We'd love your help creating new C-STREAM lessons! Follow these steps:

    1. Fork the Repository
      Fork this repository to your own GitHub account.

    2. Create a New Branch
      Create a branch specific to your changes: 

      git checkout -b add-new-lesson-plan

    3. Use Our Templates
      Build your lesson using the C-STREAM Lesson Plan Template. Ensure your lesson:

    4. Integrates faith and reason (the "R" in C-STREAM)
    5. Specifies grade-appropriate timing (K: 25min, 1-2: 30min, 3-4: 40min, 5-6: 45min)
    6. Includes materials from the CSCOE Library where applicable

    7. Connects to Catholic values and/or Catholic Social Teaching

    8. Submit a Pull Request
      Submit a pull request to the main branch with a clear description of your lesson.

    3. ✨ Improving Existing Resources¶

    If you have suggestions for improving current materials:

    1. Identify the Resource
      Locate the file in the appropriate folder (Templates/, Rubrics/, Resources/)

    2. Fork and Branch
      Fork the repository and create a branch

    3. Make Changes
      Edit to improve clarity, expand activities, or better integrate Catholic values. Be sure to reference:

    4. CSCOE Library materials where appropriate
    5. Grade-level time frames

    6. The 12 Success Factors outlined in the framework

    7. Submit a Pull Request
      Include a description of what you changed and why

    4. 👨‍🔬 Adding Catholic Scientist Profiles¶

    Help expand our Catholic Scientists Heritage resource:

    1. Research a Catholic scientist not yet profiled
    2. Include:
    3. Biographical information
    4. Scientific contributions
    5. Faith journey and how faith influenced their work
    6. Discussion questions for students
    7. Grade-level adaptations

    5. 📦 Contributing CSCOE Library Integration¶

    If you have experience with CSCOE Library materials:

    • Share lesson ideas using specific equipment

    • Document setup procedures for materials

    • Suggest alternative activities when materials aren't available

    ✅ Contribution Guidelines¶

    Respect Catholic Values¶

    All lesson plans, resources, and materials must align with Catholic values and teachings. C-STREAM is built on the foundation that faith and reason are complementary.

    Maintain Grade Appropriateness¶

    Grade Time Approach
    Kindergarten 25 min Wonder, exploration, simple hands-on
    Grades 1-2 30 min Guided exploration with structure
    Grades 3-4 40 min Independent work with collaboration
    Grades 5-6 45 min Complex projects, student-led inquiry

    Follow the 12 Success Factors¶

    Ensure contributions align with the 12 Success Factors for Catholic STEM education.

    Use Consistent Formatting¶

    • Follow existing file naming conventions

    • Use provided templates

    • Include proper YAML frontmatter

    • Add breadcrumb navigation

    Test Your Contributions¶

    If contributing a new lesson plan:

    • Test in a classroom setting if possible

    • Note any challenges or modifications needed

    • Include setup time and preparation requirements

    Also provide exact, scalable supplies for 10/15/20/25 students, numbered steps within the native period, an individual objective-linked evidence check, visible safety/stop rules, support/challenge, cleanup and an indoor alternative when weather matters. For early readers, demonstrate directions and accept oral, drawn or manipulated evidence.

    Use hands-on/unplugged methods first. Categorize technology as None, Optional, Recommended or Required and explain any required use. A device-free fallback must state what changes in the objective; it cannot certify actual hardware/software execution. Family work and donations must not be prerequisites.

    Update the curriculum maps¶

    Add/update the corresponding band-audit CSV in Review/ for every lesson. Use the documented schema, the actual schedule/rotation, the native period as integer minutes per meeting, and 2-5 relevant local codes linked to planned individual evidence. Keep the baseline status/priority and record the subsequent revision separately.

    From the repository root:

    .\scripts\Build-CurriculumMaps.ps1
.\scripts\Build-CurriculumMaps.ps1 -ValidateOnly
mkdocs build

    Include the regenerated maps with the curriculum change. Schema validation does not establish safety, developmental fit or standards mastery. Report desk walkthroughs and actual classroom trials separately.

    For current Kindergarten version-3.0 references, keep metadata, actual teaching steps and the individual-evidence definitions in the K sync script consistent:

    .\scripts\Sync-KindergartenAudit.ps1
.\scripts\Test-KindergartenReferences.ps1
.\scripts\Build-CurriculumMaps.ps1

    The K validator checks the current 37-document/29-autonomous-reference contract, 25-minute sequences and supply scaling. An intentional structural revision must update the corresponding contract/tests, not merely bypass their failures.

    Verify sources and claims¶

    Use authoritative sources and record the URL, applicable version and review date. Official benchmark alignment needs the exact benchmark, student task and assessment evidence. Label locally created standards as local. Unverified Church/history/Archdiocesan/state/accreditation claims are VERIFICATION REQUIRED; do not invent identifiers or quotations.

    Integrate Faith Meaningfully¶

    Don't just add a prayer at the beginning—weave Catholic identity throughout like "yeast that causes everything to rise."

    🔄 Review Process¶

    Once your pull request is submitted:

    1. Initial Review - The C-STREAM team reviews your contribution
    2. Feedback - You may receive suggestions for improvements
    3. Revision - Update your pull request based on feedback
    4. Merge - Approved contributions are merged into the main branch
    5. Recognition - Contributors are acknowledged in release notes

    💡 Ideas for Contributions¶

    Not sure where to start? Here are some ideas:

    • Add more Catholic scientist profiles

    • Create grade-specific activity variations

    • Develop Digital Art/Music integration lessons

    • Write family engagement activities

    • Translate resources to Spanish

    • Create video tutorials for complex setups

    • Document CSCOE equipment procedures

    • Develop assessment tools

    • Add seasonal/liturgical connections

    📫 Questions?¶

    If you have questions about contributing:

    • Open a Discussion in the repository

    • Review existing Issues for similar questions

    • Contact the C-STREAM team through GitHub

    🙏 Thank You!¶

    Your contributions help us continue to inspire students to explore STEM through a Catholic lens. Together, we can help students see how science and faith work together to understand God's amazing creation.

    "Science and faith are complementary – the beautiful harmony of faith and reason so students can be a light in the secular world."

    Happy Teaching and Creating! ✨
